properties.name: Courtland Place
properties.description: Houston's premier grand residential boulevard enclave, planned in 1906 by S.E. Gideon with monumental brick entrance gates, majestic palm trees, and landmark estates designed by Birdsall Briscoe and John Staub.

properties.name: Main Street / Market Square
properties.description: The historic civic and commercial heart of 19th-century Houston surrounding the original 1836 town square, featuring Texas's finest collection of Victorian commercial brick storefronts and early financial institutions.

properties.name: West Eleventh Place
properties.description: A secluded residential cul-de-sac enclave designed in 1920 by noted architect Maurice J. Sullivan, featuring distinctive English cottage and Craftsman residences set along private brick gardens.

properties.name: Westmoreland
properties.description: Planned in 1902 as Houston's first elite master-planned streetcar suburb south of downtown, characterized by wide esplanades, stone carriage blocks, and ornate transitional Victorian and Craftsman homes.

properties.name: Old Sixth Ward
properties.description: Houston's oldest intact residential neighborhood, settled in the 1850s by German and rail worker families, preserving the greatest concentration of 19th-century Victorian cottages and gingerbread trim in the southern United States.

properties.name: Avondale East
properties.description: An early 20th-century residential streetcar subdivision in Montrose developed between 1907 and 1925, distinguished by grand American Foursquare residences, Craftsman woodwork, and wide front verandas.

properties.name: Norhill
properties.description: A beloved master-planned 1920s neighborhood developed by Will Hogg's Varner Realty Co., celebrated for its dense rows of intact Craftsman bungalows with exposed rafter tails, bracketed eaves, and Proctor Plaza Park.

properties.name: Broadacres
properties.description: A landmark planned park-like residential community developed in the 1920s by Capt. James A. Baker and prominent Houston leaders, designed by architect William Ward Watkin with wide oak-lined boulevards and monumental estates.

properties.name: Avondale West
properties.description: The western continuation of Montrose's historic Avondale subdivision along Lovett and Stratford streets, featuring well-preserved Craftsman bungalows and two-story brick and timber residences.

properties.name: Houston Heights West
properties.description: The western sector of Houston's premier 1891 streetcar suburb, developed by the Omaha and South Texas Land Company, showcasing picturesque Victorian turrets, wraparound porches, and Craftsman streetscapes.

properties.name: Houston Heights East
properties.description: The eastern residential sector of the Heights along Harvard and Cortlandt streets, lined with magnificent turn-of-the-century Victorian residences, shady oak trees, and historic neighborhood churches.

properties.name: Freeland
properties.description: A charming and compact residential enclave in Near Northside platted in the 1920s, consisting of intact modest Craftsman bungalows built for middle-class rail and industrial workers.

properties.name: Shadow Lawn
properties.description: A prestigious cul-de-sac enclave bordering Rice University and Hermann Park, platted in 1923 by Homer D. Torrey, featuring architect-designed revival manors and stately live oaks.

properties.name: Audubon Place
properties.description: An elegant Montrose subdivision platted in 1910 along Audubon, Kipling, and Marshall streets, famous for its wide palm- and oak-lined streets and impressive collection of Craftsman and Prairie-style residences.

properties.name: Boulevard Oaks
properties.description: World-renowned for its cathedral live oak canopy along North and South Boulevards, planned in the 1920s by landscape architect William L. Phillips with extraordinary period revival residences.

properties.name: First Montrose Commons
properties.description: A diverse historic neighborhood in southern Montrose between West Alabama and Richmond, featuring a rich variety of early 1900s Victorian cottages, American Foursquares, and Craftsman duplexes.

properties.name: Houston Heights South
properties.description: The southern gateway to the Heights bounded by 11th Street and I-10, encompassing the Heights Boulevard historic esplanade, Victorian mansions, and early commercial storefronts.

properties.name: Woodland Heights
properties.description: Developed in 1907 by William A. Wilson along the Houston Electric Company streetcar line, featuring rolling topography, proximity to Stude and White Oak Parks, and pristine Craftsman bungalows.

properties.name: Glenbrook Valley
properties.description: The largest designated mid-century modern historic district in the state of Texas and one of the largest in the nation, developed between 1953 and 1962 with stunning custom Atomic Era and Mid-Century Modern ranch estates.

properties.name: Germantown
properties.description: Platted in 1894 along Little White Oak Bayou by German immigrant families, retaining modest late 19th-century frame cottages, brick streets, and deep vernacular community ties.

properties.name: Starkweather
properties.description: A historic residential enclave in Independence Heights, established during the Jim Crow era as Texas's first incorporated Black municipality, preserving vernacular frame cottages and shotgun structures.

properties.name: High First Ward
properties.description: A historic working-class neighborhood northwest of downtown near the Southern Pacific rail yards, retaining early Victorian cottages, corner grocery structures, and immigrant artisan homes.

properties.name: Brunner-Harmonium
properties.description: Houston's newest historic district, located in the historic West End/Washington Avenue corridor, preserving vernacular 1890s-1920s railroad worker homes and historic church structures.

properties.name: Freedmen's Town
properties.description: Settled in 1865 by formerly enslaved people upon Juneteenth emancipation, Freedmen's Town served as the cultural, educational, and commercial center of Black Houston, featuring hand-laid brick streets, historic churches, and shotgun cottages.

properties.name: Idylwood (NRHP)
properties.description: A picturesque 1920s-1930s residential subdivision in Houston's East End bordering Brays Bayou, noted for its hilly topography, winding streets, and dense Tudor Revival masonry bungalows.

properties.name: Independence Heights (NRHP)
properties.full_name: Independence Heights National Register Historic District
properties.description: The first incorporated African American municipality in Texas (incorporated 1915), documenting the resilience, civic independence, and architectural history of early 20th-century Black Texans.

properties.name: Near Northside (NRHP)
properties.full_name: Near Northside National Register Historic District
properties.description: A historic rail and industrial community north of Buffalo Bayou with deep working-class roots, European immigrant settlement, and later Mexican-American cultural heritage.
